question: Three candidates, and every voter has rational, consistent preferences. Can a majority end up preferring A over B, a majority prefer B over C, and yet a majority also prefer C over A?
choices: No — majority preferences can never form such a loop
Yes — the group's majority preferences really can loop like that
anchorText: a majority of voters will prefer A to B, B to C, and also C to A

question: A breathalyzer never fails to catch a truly drunk driver, and wrongly flags a sober driver only 5% of the time. About 1 in 1,000 drivers is actually drunk. A randomly stopped driver tests positive — how likely is it they're really drunk?

question: Earth generates its own magnetic field. Exactly one moon in the Solar System is known to generate one internally. Which moon?
anchorText: Ganymede is the only natural satellite in the solar system to possess an internally generated magnetic field
